official.description_text:
Postdoc in cyber-physical security for smart grids
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
As power systems become more digitalised and rely increasingly on synchronised measurements, protecting monitoring data and communications is essential for reliable grid operation. The research will focus on threats such as time-synchronisation attacks and manipulation of monitoring data in wide-area monitoring systems, characterization of their impact on system operation, and their timely detection using machine learning algorithms. The postdoc will develop methods for detection and resilience, and collaborate with an international team to validate them in cyber-physical power-system scenarios.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made
Strong publication track record in leading conferences and/or journals in a relevant research field
As the work involves international cooperation, excellent skills in English are required, both oral and in writing
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience with simulation-based on experimental validation
The ability to work in a team as well as independently
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Name and email address of two references.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in cyber-physical security for electrical power systems, focusing on detection of time-synchronisation attacks and monitoring-data manipulation in wide-area monitoring systems using machine learning, with experimental validation in power-system scenarios.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position focuses on power-grid cybersecurity, attack detection algorithms, and critical infrastructure resilience. The researcher's core domains are human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, and collaborative design. There is no thematic overlap. The domain is cyber-physical security for infrastructure, not human-computer interaction or immersive systems.

methodological_fit.rationale: The position emphasises machine learning algorithms for anomaly detection, simulation-based validation, and experimental testing. The researcher has beginner-level Python skills and intermediate quantitative-research methods. However, the required expertise is in machine learning (algorithms, training, validation), power-system simulation software, and cybersecurity domain knowledge—none of which are evidenced in the profile. While both domains value experimental validation, the contexts diverge completely.

growth_value.rationale: Pursuing machine learning for power-grid security would develop some algorithmic and statistical capabilities, but these do not close gaps in human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition evaluation, or collaborative design. The growth is in a tangential domain (security ML) rather than the target trajectory.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is not a priority-1 institution for the researcher; Sweden is a preferred country (secondary ranking). The School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at KTH is well-regarded, and the postdoc is externally funded. However, the position sits in power-systems cybersecurity, not HCI or XR research communities. Early-career credibility built here would not translate to target domains or networks.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD or equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last 3 years preferred. Researcher is MSc by Research stage; must complete MSc and PhD before eligibility.
Position is postdoc (not doctoral-researcher or entry-level). Researcher must first complete both MSc and PhD to become eligible.

Position may require security clearance under Swedish Protective Security Act (2018:585) due to critical infrastructure sensitivity. Researcher's nationality (Malaysian) and residency may affect clearance eligibility; note ambiguous/unconfirmed nationality restrictions.
English proficiency required; researcher's profile indicates fluency suitable for academic work.
risks: This is a postdoc position. Researcher is currently at MSc stage; must complete both MSc and PhD before eligibility—timeline unclear.
Major disciplinary pivot from HCI-XR to cyber-physical security for power grids; would signal departure from core target identity.
Requires machine learning expertise (algorithm design, model training, validation) beyond researcher's beginner-level Python and no demonstrated ML background.
Security clearance requirement for critical infrastructure role may impose restrictions on researcher mobility or future employment, particularly for non-EU researchers.
2-year postdoc commitment in power-systems security delays integration into HCI-XR research networks and PhD community building in target area.
